subject: Dedicated capacity recap — reserved GPUs, isolation needs, scaling plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Timothy Blake <t.blake@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap — reserved GPUs, isolation needs, scaling plan

Hi Tim — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Pain points you shared:
- Latency spikes and tail latency during morning peak (08:00–10:30 PT) for clinical-question-answering flows (~25% of calls hit >600ms).
- Unpredictable unit costs on shared endpoints when traffic from other tenants bursts.
- Data residency and isolation requirements for PHI-adjacent inference (need dedicated tenancy and audit logs).

Goals you articulated:
- Stable p95 latency <= 300ms for typical chat/QA workloads.
- Dedicated GPU pool to guarantee capacity during peak hours.
- SOC 2 evidence and KMS integration for key material.

Proposed Dedicated capacity plan (high-level):
- Reserved pool: 4x A40-equivalent GPUs initially (can be reserved as dedicated slots in our Dedicated offering).
- Autoscaling buffer: +2 GPU burst capacity for sustained spikes (cross-account throttling disabled for these nodes).
- Model runtime: quantized variant of the 13B model you mentioned (we estimate ~60 qps aggregate with request batching).
- Isolation: VPC peering + tenant-level disk encryption; audit logging enabled with 90-day retention (longer retention available as add-on).
- SLA targets: 99.5% uptime for Dedicated pool, p95 latency target of <=300ms under typical request distribution (we'll validate with an initial load test).

Open items we agreed to action:
1) You to confirm peak concurrent requests and average request size so we can finalize GPU count (Tim).
2) Redwood to run an initial capacity sizing with your sample traffic (Marissa + Vivek).
3) Legal/procurement touchpoint for standard SOW and reserved capacity terms (Tim).

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-proposal-acme-20260305.pdf (proposal + pricing), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

Proposed next meeting: 30–45 min sizing + security sync (include Vivek) — are you available Mon 3/8 or Tue 3/9 between 9–12 PT?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
m: (415) 555-0142
marissa@redwood.ai
From: Timothy Blake <t.blake@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap — reserved GPUs, isolation needs, scaling plan

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Peak: about 400 concurrent inference sessions during morning peak; average request payload ~1.2KB, typical response ~3–4KB.
- Models: we'll prioritize the 13B family for now, may add a smaller embedding-only model later.
- Data residency: all inference must run in our region (us-west-2). Can Dedicated be provisioned in that region?
- Procurement: procurement/legal will need estimated MRR and a simple statement of work. Procurement contact: Sara Nguyen (sara.nguyen@acmehealth.com).

Also: can you attach the SOC2 summary you mentioned? They'll want a quick PDF for their security review.

I can do Mon 3/8 9:30–10:15 PT — that works for a sizing call with an infra/solutions engineer.

Thanks,
Timothy Blake
Director, ML Platforms | Acme Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Timothy Blake <t.blake@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap — reserved GPUs, isolation needs, scaling plan

Perfect — thanks for the details, Tim. Answers inline and next steps: 

- Region: yes, we can provision Dedicated capacity in us-west-2. We'll scope the initial pool there.
- Sizing: based on 400 concurrent sessions and your payloads, our quick estimate still points to 4 reserved A40-equivalents with autoscale +2 for headroom; we'll validate with load test.
- SOC2: attaching redwood-soc2-summary.pdf here and linking to our compliance page in the HubSpot deal (see related_links).
- Procurement: noted Sara Nguyen — can you intro Sara on this thread or send procurement contact details and timing?

Action items for our side:
- Vivek to run a short load/sizing test next week with a representative traffic trace (Vivek, can you confirm availability Mon 3/8 9:30 PT?).
- I'll prepare a simple SOW and MRR estimate and share ahead of the call (attaching a draft pricing table in the proposal).

Meeting: confirmed Mon 3/8 9:30–10:15 PT for sizing + security sync. I'll send calendar invite.

Cheers,
Marissa
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity recap — quick internal alignment

Looping you both for the scoping test: Vivek — please prioritize a 30–60 minute sizing run with Tim's trace on Mon morning. Focus checklist:
- Validate p95 latency with batching disabled and with conservative batching (we need both numbers).
- Verify KV cache behavior across dedicated pool and ensure no cross-tenant leakage.
- Confirm audit log export to S3 bucket in us-west-2 and KMS key handshake.

I'll draft the SOW language for the MRR commit and include a clause for burst capacity. Marissa — send me the preliminary pricing table and I'll format for legal.

-Rafael
